t: Tom left on a Tuesday, came home from work, didn't take off his coat.
18 months later, I flew business class to Barcelona by myself.
I'm leaving. I've met someone.
What?
Her name's Amy.
How old is she?
Claire, it's...
How old?
After Tom left, the house went quiet. Then my daughter Emma called.
Mum, are you sure you're okay?
I'm fine, love.
It's just... Dad said you've never really been independent.
Have you paid the electric bill? Do you know how to do that?
I'm 55, Emma. I have a master's degree. I managed budgets for 15 years.
I know. I'm just asking.
A few days later, I went to book club and pretended everything was normal.
She was so dependent on him. I honestly don't know how she's going to survive.
I'll show you what survival looks like. The next morning, I called Andrea and asked her to meet me.
When did you stop wearing lipstick? What has that got to do with anything?
I've watched a lot of women come through a divorce. The ones still wearing color,
still taking up space with their faces, they come back faster.
When, Claire?
I don't know. It wasn't a decision. It was a slow erosion.
Tom said once that the color looked like I was trying too hard.
There are 30-something tubes in my bathroom drawer. I haven't touched them in years.

Hyaluronic acid, squilline. My lips at 60 are softer than they were at 48.
Does it bleed into the lines? It can't. The color comes from underneath your own skin.

For the first eight seconds, nothing. Then slowly, very slowly, a color started to develop.
I haven't seen this color on my mouth in 20 years.
Nothing. The color was soft, warm, and for the first time in years, I liked what I saw.
Six weeks later, I booked a flight to Barcelona business class.
Traveling on your own today? I am.
Enjoy Barcelona. I intend to.
Excuse me, are you here alone? I am.
So are we. Would you like to join us? Yes, I would.
Is this your first solo trip? It is. How does it feel?
Like I've been holding my breath for 28 years. And I finally exhaled.
I have to ask you something. What are you wearing on your lips?
It's called Kevora. How long have you had it on? Since 7 o'clock this morning.
For 22 years, I've been testing liver and I've never seen a formula at last 13 hours
on a woman over 50 without bleeding into the fine lines.
You know what's different about you? What?
You don't look like a woman who survived something. You look like a woman who decided something.
When I got back from Barcelona, Emma came round. She wanted to see every photograph.
Dad said you'd never be able to travel alone. Your father said a lot of things that weren't true, Emma.
You look incredible in these.
Rebecca wrote that Tom had seen the photographs and didn't know what to say.
Once that would have mattered. This time it didn't.
Tom told everyone I couldn't handle being alone.
He wasn't entirely wrong based on what I'd shown him for 28 years.
He was right about who I'd become. He was wrong about who I was.
The lipstick didn't make me capable, but it made me decide every morning for six weeks
that I was a woman worth looking at. I wasn't surviving. I was thriving.
